metaDescription: Six drip and single-serve coffee makers at or under $25, compared on capacity, pause-and-serve, filters and auto shutoff for dorms, desks and small kitchens.
introParagraphs: A coffee maker at the very bottom of the price range has one job: heat water, drip it through grounds and hand you a cup. There are no grinders, no app controls and no thermal carafes, and that is exactly the appeal for a dorm room, a camper, an office desk or a guest room.

The six machines here are all simple. Five are drip makers in sizes from four cups up to twelve, and one is a single-serve brewer that fills a travel mug. What differs is capacity, whether the machine has a reusable filter, whether it can pause mid-brew and whether it shuts itself off. We evaluated each from the listing specs and buyer feedback, with no claims of bench testing.

Cheap machines can still brew a decent pot if you respect a few basics: fresh grounds, clean water and a regular wash. We also point out the small design differences that make a machine easier to live with, such as a water window or a no-drip spout, because those are the details that decide whether you keep using it. At this level, nothing is built to last a decade, so the smart move is to buy for the routine you have now, treat the machine as a replaceable tool and spend any saved effort on better beans and a good scoop rather than on features you will rarely touch.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 12-Cup Coffee Maker with Easy On/Off Switch
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER is the largest machine here, built for households that go through a pot of coffee in a morning. It brews up to 12 cups, and the Vortex showerhead spreads water across the grounds so they are evenly saturated. A simple on and off switch and a removable filter basket keep operation uncomplicated.

The Sneak-A-Cup feature briefly stops the flow so you can pour a cup before the pot finishes, and the carafe spout is designed to pour without dripping down the side. Those two details solve the most common annoyances of cheap coffee makers: a messy pour and waiting for the cycle to end. The tradeoff is size, as a 12-cup machine is not a compact choice for a tiny counter.

Compared with the 5-cup Elite Gourmet machines, it makes more coffee than a small household needs. Next to the Amazon Basics at 5 cups, it is better suited to guests and families. If you want one machine for a busy household without spending more, it is the most capable here.
products.bestFor: Families and guests who need a full pot at once.

Showerhead wets grounds evenly

Non-drip spout keeps the counter clean
cons: Large footprint for a small counter
Too much coffee for one or two people

products.name: Amazon Basics 5-Cup Drip Coffee Maker with Glass Carafe
products.description:
Amazon Basics sells this 5-cup machine with a modern look and the one safety feature many cheap coffee makers lack: a built-in 2-hour automatic shutoff. The glass pot holds 0.8 quarts, and an auto pause lets you pour a cup while it is still brewing, then resumes when the pot returns.

The automatic shutoff matters to anyone who has left the house wondering whether the burner is still on. The compact 5-cup size is sensible for one or two coffee drinkers, and the removable filter basket is simple to rinse. It does not state a reusable filter, so expect to buy paper filters.

Compared with the Elite Gourmet EHC9420 at 5 cups, it adds the shutoff safeguard. Against the BLACK+DECKER at 12 cups, it is smaller and cheaper to run for a household of one or two. It is the best choice for a first apartment or a bedroom where forgetting to unplug a machine is a real risk.
products.bestFor: Forgetful mornings and first apartments where safety matters.
pros: Built-in two hour automatic shutoff
Auto pause allows a mid-brew cup
Compact 0.8 qt pot fits small counters
Modern styling suits any kitchen
cons: Basic controls with no brew strength option

products.name: Elite Gourmet EHC9420 5-Cup Drip Coffee Maker
products.description:
Elite Gourmet designs the EHC9420 for personal use, couples and small households. It brews up to 5 cups, includes a reusable filter housed in a swing-out basket, and offers Pause N Serve for a quick pour in the middle of a cycle.

The swing-out basket is a thoughtful detail, because it makes filling and cleaning easier than a drop-in design. A reusable filter also cuts down on paper filters, which saves a small amount over time and avoids running out. The tradeoff is that mesh filters let a touch of sediment through compared with paper, so the cup can be slightly more full-bodied.

Compared with the Amazon Basics, it lacks an automatic shutoff in the listing, so you must unplug it yourself. Next to the EHC-5055, it is nearly a twin, and the choice depends on finish and availability. It is a good pick for budget buyers who want to avoid paper filters.
products.bestFor: Couples who want to skip paper filters entirely.

Swing-out basket is easy to fill

products.name: Elite Gourmet EHC-5055 5-Cup Brew and Drip Coffee Maker
products.description:
The EHC-5055 is the second 5-cup Elite Gourmet in this guide, with a semi-transparent reservoir and a level indicator that shows how much water is ready for brewing. It includes Pause N Serve, a reusable filter and an on and off switch.

The water level window is the feature that makes it easy to measure without a separate jug, which helps new coffee drinkers get the ratio right. Everything else is the same philosophy as its sibling: plain, quick and cheap. The listing includes unrelated text about espresso grind and pressure, which suggests copy shared across models, so treat it as a straightforward drip machine.

Next to the EHC9420, it offers a similar feature set and a slightly different body. Against the four-cup EHC4128, it brews one cup more. It makes sense for a dorm or a desk where you want a no-surprises machine that tells you how much water is in it.

products.name: Elite Gourmet EHC4128 4-Cup Drip Coffee Maker
products.description:
At four cups, the EHC4128 is the smallest drip machine in this group and the best fit for a single drinker who wants a refill or two. It has a glass carafe, a semi-transparent reservoir with a level indicator, a reusable filter and Pause N Serve.

Small size means fewer grounds wasted on a pot nobody finishes, which is how many people use a cheap coffee maker. It also fits on a crowded shelf or a camper counter more easily than a 12-cup model. As with the other Elite Gourmet machines, controls are minimal, so there is nothing to learn but also nothing to customize.

Compared with the 5-cup Amazon Basics, it brews one cup less and skips the shutoff timer. Against the EHC113M single-serve, it makes a small pot rather than a single mug. It is the right choice when you want a classic glass pot in the smallest footprint.
products.bestFor: Solo drinkers who want a small glass pot.
pros: Smallest drip footprint in the group
Glass carafe with Pause N Serve
Reusable filter avoids paper purchases

cons: Only four cups per brew cycle at most
No automatic shutoff in the listing

products.name: Elite Gourmet EHC113M Personal Single-Serve Coffee Maker
products.description:
The EHC113M takes a different approach: a personal brewer that makes one mug at a time. It includes a 14 oz insulated travel mug with a stainless 304 interior, so you brew straight into the mug and head out the door. The listing promises a brew in under 60 seconds, and a 600W heater with one-touch operation keeps things fast.

There are no paper pods or capsules, which cuts waste, and the compact form suits a desk, dorm or car commute. You trade away the ability to serve more than one person, and the 14 oz mug limits how much you get per brew. The mint finish also adds some personality to a plain appliance.

Compared with the EHC4128 four-cup pot, it is faster and more mobile but cannot fill a carafe for guests. Against the BLACK+DECKER at 12 cups, it is a single-person solution. It is ideal for a commuter or a student who wants a quick mug rather than a pot.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cup sizes on coffee makers use a small unit, so a 5-cup pot yields roughly two to three regular mugs. The BLACK+DECKER brews up to 12 cups, the Amazon Basics and two Elite Gourmet models make 5, and the EHC4128 makes 4. For one drinker, a smaller pot wastes less. For a household with guests, 12 cups is more practical. As a quick rule, count your mugs per day, divide by two and add one: that number tells you roughly how many machine cups you actually need, and anything beyond it is coffee that goes cold on the plate.

Pause and serve lets you slide the pot away mid-brew to pour a cup, because a valve stops the drip. The Elite Gourmet models call it Pause N Serve, the Amazon Basics calls it auto pause and the BLACK+DECKER calls it Sneak-A-Cup. If you are always in a rush in the morning, this feature is more valuable than a long list of extras. Remember that pouring early gives you a stronger first cup, because the last of the brew is more dilute, so give the pot a gentle swirl once it finishes to even things out.

A shutoff turns the warming plate off after a set time, protecting against forgetting. The Amazon Basics lists a 2-hour automatic shutoff, which is the only explicit one here. If you do not have one, make a habit of switching off the machine at the wall before leaving. A switched power strip makes this effortless, and it also stops the standby draw that small appliances quietly add over a year of daily use.

Reusable mesh filters save on paper filters and are included with the Elite Gourmet drip models. Paper filters trap more oils and fine sediment, which gives a cleaner cup. If you prefer a lighter taste, buy paper filters even if a reusable one is included. Whichever you choose, rinse the basket straight after brewing, because stale oils from yesterday's grounds are the most common cause of a bitter cup.

A clear reservoir with level marks removes guesswork. The EHC4128 and EHC-5055 have semi-transparent reservoirs with indicators. Without them you rely on the carafe markings, which is fine but easy to misread when half asleep. Fill with cold water, never hot, and measure grounds with a level scoop so a pot made on a groggy morning tastes the same as one made on a calm Sunday.

A badly shaped spout drips down the side and onto the counter. The BLACK+DECKER advertises a no-drip pour spout, which is a real quality-of-life improvement over a plain glass lip. Always pour steadily and keep the lid closed to reduce spills.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brewing convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared pause features and fill aids. The BLACK+DECKER's Sneak-A-Cup, the Amazon Basics' auto pause and the Elite Gourmet Pause N Serve all earned credit, and the single-serve EHC113M scored for one-touch brewing.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and shutoff
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked for automatic shutoff and basic safeguards. The Amazon Basics stood out with a 2-hour automatic shutoff, while others scored lower where the listing did not mention one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched capacity to the likely user: the 4-cup EHC4128 and single-serve EHC113M for individuals, the 5-cup models for couples and the 12-cup BLACK+DECKER for families.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filters and cleanup
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered filter type and basket design. The Elite Gourmet reusable filters and swing-out basket reduce ongoing purchases, and the removable baskets on the BLACK+DECKER and Amazon Basics simplify cleaning.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value at the lowest cap
howWeEvaluated.description: We asked what each machine does well for its tiny price. Small refinements such as a no-drip spout or a level window counted for more than raw capacity. We also treated the single-serve format as its own case instead of ranking it against pots, since a mug brewer and a 12-cup machine are bought for entirely different reasons.

faq.q: Which coffee maker under this cap is best overall?
faq.a: The BLACK+DECKER 12-Cup is the most capable because of its Vortex showerhead, Sneak-A-Cup pause and non-drip spout. If you drink alone or want safety, the Amazon Basics 5-Cup with its 2-hour shutoff is the better small-household choice.

faq.q: How many cups does a 5-cup machine really make?
faq.a: Machine cup measures are smaller than a mug, so five cups usually fill two to three regular mugs. The Amazon Basics lists 0.8 qt for its pot. Check the carafe markings to see how much your favorite mug takes.

faq.q: Are reusable filters better than paper?
faq.a: They save money and avoid paper waste, but they let more fine sediment and oils through. Paper filters give a cleaner cup. Elite Gourmet models include reusable filters, and you can still use paper in most baskets if you prefer.

faq.q: How do I clean a cheap drip machine?
faq.a: Wash the carafe and basket after each use and run a vinegar and water cycle about once a month to remove scale. Follow with two clean water cycles to clear the taste. Mineral buildup slows brewing and dulls flavor.

faq.q: Is a single-serve brewer cheaper to run?
faq.a: It avoids wasting a full pot when you only want one mug, and the Elite Gourmet EHC113M needs no pods. You still buy grounds, but you control the quantity. For one drinker it often wastes less coffee.

faq.q: Why does my coffee taste weak from a cheap machine?
faq.a: Low-cost machines can brew slightly cool, so use fresh grounds, the right ratio and cold filtered water. A showerhead like the BLACK+DECKER's helps saturation. Also run a hot water cycle first to warm the machine.

faq.q: Is it safe to leave the machine on the warming plate?
faq.a: Short periods are normal, but leaving it on for hours scorches the coffee and wastes energy. The Amazon Basics has a 2-hour shutoff, while others rely on you to switch them off. Unplug a machine you will not use for a while. If you often want a second cup later, pour the finished pot into a vacuum flask instead of leaving it on the plate, since a flask keeps flavor far better than a hot plate does.
